title: LIBERO: Benchmarking Knowledge Transfer for Lifelong Robot Learning
tldr: Procedurally generated manipulation benchmark with four suites (130 tasks) plus teleoperated demos, originally for lifelong learning; its Spatial/Object/Goal/Long suites became the de facto VLA success-rate benchmark on which most VLA acceleration papers report.
relevance_reason: Seed benchmark; the standard testbed where efficiency methods report accuracy retention.

title: LIBERO-Para: A Diagnostic Benchmark and Metrics for Paraphrase Robustness in VLA Models
tldr: LIBERO variant that paraphrases action verbs and object references; seven VLAs (0.6B-7.5B) lose 22-52 points, mostly from object synonym changes, and a difficulty-weighted metric (PRIDE) is proposed.
relevance_reason: Robustness variant of LIBERO; relevant to whether compressed VLAs retain language grounding.

title: LIBERO-VPro: Benchmarking Closed-Loop Visual Robustness of Robotic Foundation Models
tldr: Closed-loop visual-robustness benchmark on LIBERO with degradation, stale-camera, source-consistency and scene-change perturbations; ~196k sim episodes plus 200 real rollouts show VLAs and world-action models are very sensitive to stale or missing frames.
relevance_reason: Camera staleness perturbation directly probes latency/asynchrony effects that efficiency methods introduce.

title: LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
tldr: Parametric LIBERO-based benchmark for physical and semantic safety with ~19.7k collision-free demos; evaluation of eight VLAs finds a tension between generalization and safe execution.
relevance_reason: Adds safety axis to LIBERO evaluation; relevant for deployability metrics.

title: LIBERO-PRO: Towards Robust and Fair Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Models Beyond Memorization
tldr: Shows that VLAs scoring >90% on standard LIBERO drop to ~0% when objects, initial states, instructions or environments are perturbed, arguing LIBERO rewards rote memorization.
relevance_reason: Seed robustness variant; implies LIBERO success retention is a weak signal for judging compressed/accelerated VLAs.

title: LIBERO-RECOVER: Beyond Task Success Towards Failure Recovery in Robotic Manipulation Models
tldr: Benchmark of 1000+ failure states harvested from real policy failures on LIBERO across four recovery levels, measuring whether VLAs/WAMs can recover rather than just succeed from clean starts.
relevance_reason: Extends LIBERO evaluation beyond nominal success; recovery is a key deployability metric.

title: MINERVA: How Small Can a Manipulation Policy Be and Still Solve LIBERO?
reported_metric: 5-9 ms per chunk (113x faster than SmolVLA, 1400x faster than pi0.5)
tldr: A 0.54M-parameter visuomotor policy reaches 95.1% average on the four LIBERO suites, showing the benchmark needs little capacity and that task-ID conditioning mostly selects memorized tasks; robustness collapses on LIBERO-Plus.
relevance_reason: Directly questions whether LIBERO can discriminate efficient VLAs; strong methodological evidence.

title: LIBERO-VIFO: Benchmarking the Capability and Safety of Visual Cue Following in Vision-Language-Action Models
tldr: Benchmark of eight visual-cue families testing whether VLAs follow authorized cues and ignore unauthorized ones; finds VLAs often act on cues even with no language instruction.
relevance_reason: LIBERO-derived evaluation variant; tangential to efficiency.

title: LIBERO-Occ: Evaluating and Improving Vision-Language-Action Models under Scene-Induced Occlusion via Viewpoint Imagination
tldr: Occlusion-focused extension of LIBERO plus a method that imagines a second viewpoint; SOTA VLAs degrade substantially under scene-induced occlusion.
relevance_reason: LIBERO robustness variant.

title: LIBERO-X: Robustness Litmus for Vision-Language-Action Models
tldr: Rethinks LIBERO with a progressive-difficulty protocol over spatial, object and instruction generalization plus a more diverse teleoperated training set; VLAs drop sharply under cumulative perturbations.
relevance_reason: LIBERO robustness variant aimed at more reliable VLA benchmarking.

title: LIBERO-MAX: Do Robot Policies Adapt When the World Changes?
tldr: 8,000 paired episodes with and without a mid-execution event (object moves, viewpoint shift, obstacle); 14 policies lose 11-26 points, and changing re-query cadence does not close the gap.
relevance_reason: Measures reactivity to dynamic change, the property most affected by latency and chunk length; paired protocol is methodologically useful.

title: What Are We Actually Benchmarking in Robot Manipulation?
tldr: Proposes four diagnostics (shortcut solvability, significance, creeping overfitting, data-source dependence) and audits five manipulation benchmarks; LIBERO and CALVIN fail several, a 0.09B no-language probe nearly matches SOTA on LIBERO and most gains lack significance.
relevance_reason: Core methodology paper on benchmark validity; directly informs how efficiency claims should be evaluated.

title: SafeVLA-Bench: A Benchmark for the Success-Safety Gap in Vision-Language-Action Models
tldr: Post-hoc STL-based safety layer over LIBERO and RoboCasa365 reporting Succ-But-Unsafe and a violation severity index; many successful rollouts still violate safety constraints.
relevance_reason: Metric beyond success rate; useful for judging accelerated policies whose trajectories change.

title: RoboRecover: Benchmarking Robot Policy Recovery under Execution Deviations
tldr: 2,000 deviation states reconstructed by replaying action prefixes on RoboTwin and LIBERO; recovery ability is not predicted by initial-state success.
relevance_reason: New evaluation dimension for closed-loop robustness.

title: Faster and Better? Benchmark Bugs and Design Limitations Distort the Evaluation of Vision-Language-Action Acceleration
tldr: Audits why training-free VLA accelerators sometimes beat the uncompressed baseline: finds 22 bugs and 4 design limitations across seven benchmarks (permissive checkers, wrong masses), and fixing them can reverse method rankings.
relevance_reason: Directly about the validity of efficiency-method evaluation on sim benchmarks.

title: SafeManip: A Property-Driven Benchmark for Temporal Safety Evaluation in Robotic Manipulation
tldr: LTLf-based temporal safety properties with per-trigger normalized metrics, audited on seven robot foundation policies; success and safety are only weakly coupled.
relevance_reason: Complementary metric layer to success rate.

title: ConflictVLA-Bench: Benchmarking Behavioral Responses of Vision-Language-Action Models to Premise Conflicts
tldr: LIBERO-based tasks with invalid premises; eight VLAs keep pursuing original targets ('failed persistence'), showing binary outcomes are insufficient for evaluation.

relevance_reason: Hardware-normalized VLA profiling study, core to C4.
